old_summary: A suspected gastroenteritis outbreak at North View Primary School in Yishun has affected 147 pupils across multiple levels, with symptoms first reported on January 13, 2026. One pupil was hospitalised on January 17 before being discharged in stable condition the following day, while most affected students had recovered by January 18. The Singapore Food Agency, Communicable Diseases Agency, and the school issued a joint statement on January 19 confirming the investigation is ongoing, with no confirmed source yet identified. North View Primary has since sanitised classrooms and common areas, restricted school-wide gatherings, and reminded pupils to practise good hygiene. The outbreak follows a separate gastroenteritis incident at River Valley Primary School earlier in January, where 60 pupils fell ill after lunch.
new_summary:
North View Primary School in Yishun reported 147 suspected gastroenteritis cases across multiple year levels beginning January 13, 2026, with one pupil hospitalised on January 17 and discharged the following day in stable condition. By January 18, most affected pupils had recovered, according to a joint statement from the school, Singapore Food Agency (SFA), and Communicable Diseases Agency (CDA) issued on January 19.

Gastroenteritis symptoms—diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and fever—can spread through contaminated food or water, person-to-person contact, or contact with contaminated surfaces. The school implemented precautionary measures including deep cleaning and sanitisation of classrooms and common areas, minimised schoolwide gatherings, and reminded pupils to practise good hygiene and rest at home if unwell.

The outbreak occurred amid a broader pattern of gastroenteritis incidents at Singapore schools in January 2026. River Valley Primary School, which operates under a central kitchen model, reported 60 gastroenteritis cases after pupils fell ill following lunch on January 14. North View Primary does not use the centralised kitchen system, suggesting multiple sources or transmission routes across different school food management models.
old_title: 147 North View Primary pupils hit by gastroenteritis in Yishun, one hospitalised
new_title: 147 Yishun primary pupils struck by gastroenteritis outbreak

old_summary: A fire broke out at a Yishun HDB flat, forcing the evacuation of approximately 50 residents and sending one occupant to hospital. The blaze triggered a large-scale emergency response, with residents from surrounding units cleared from the block as a precaution. The affected resident was taken to hospital, though the severity of injuries has not been confirmed. Fires in Yishun HDB blocks have historically drawn significant community concern given the density of the estate, and this incident is no exception.
new_summary:
A fire broke out in a second-floor unit at Block 510B Yishun Street 51 at around 3am on April 12, 2026, prompting the evacuation of about 50 residents as a precautionary measure. Members of the public extinguished the flames using a hosereel and fire extinguisher before Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) officers arrived on scene. One resident was hospitalised at Singapore General Hospital; the cause remains under investigation.

Two residents, Razie and Furzan, were credited with rescuing an affected neighbour from the fire. Nee Soon GRC MP Lee Hui Ying commended their bravery and decisive action in a Facebook post, describing their intervention as exemplary community spirit. The town council and grassroots teams have pledged ongoing support to the affected family, including assistance with cleaning and painting works. SCDF said it would reach out to commend members of the public for their public-spirited response.
old_title: Fire tears through Yishun HDB flat, 1 hospitalised and 50 evacuated
new_title: Yishun residents rescue neighbour from Block 510B fire, 50 evacuated

old_summary: Crow culling operations have resumed across nine districts in Singapore, with Yishun selected as the opening salvo in the latest round of government-sanctioned bird management. The programme, carried out by licensed shooters on behalf of authorities, targets crow populations deemed disruptive to residents and public hygiene. Yishun's selection as the first district is unlikely to surprise anyone familiar with the estate's reputation as ground zero for the unusual. No human injuries were reported, though the crows were unavailable for comment.
new_summary:
The National Parks Board (NParks) has resumed crow shooting operations in Yishun on March 24, 2026, marking the first culling since 2020. Minister for National Development Chee Hong Tat announced the resumption after six years of relying solely on trapping, nest removal, and food source reduction—measures that proved inadequate as crow-related complaints surged to 15,000 in 2025, triple the 2020 figure, and reported attacks quadrupled to over 2,000 cases.

Operations will expand across nine districts—Bishan, Jurong, Kranji, Punggol, Sembawang, Tampines, Toa Payoh, Woodlands, and Yishun—over the coming weeks. NParks has implemented strict safety protocols including cordoned shooting zones, clear signage, and auxiliary police officers deployed on-site to manage public access and prevent incidents like those that halted the previous programme, when pellets struck nearby homes.

House crows, an invasive non-native species, are highly protective of their young and prone to attacking when they perceive threats. NParks removed nearly 9,000 nests islandwide in 2025 and trapped over 13,000 birds, yet the population continued to surge. The minister urged residents to stop feeding pest birds and dispose of food scraps properly to support the multi-pronged management strategy.
old_title: Crow shooting season opens in Yishun as culling resumes across 9 districts
new_title: Crow shooting resumes in Yishun as NParks tackles invasive bird crisis

old_summary: A man was arrested after allegedly assaulting Tower Transit staff and discharging a fire extinguisher at a Yishun bus interchange, in an incident that left workers shaken and the area blanketed in chemical powder. The attack on public transport employees escalated beyond a verbal dispute, with the suspect deploying the extinguisher as an improvised weapon against staff on duty. Police were called and the man was subsequently nabbed, with Tower Transit confirming the incident involved their personnel at the Yishun location. Assaults on public transport workers in Singapore carry enhanced penalties under the law, making this arrest particularly significant for the bus operator's staff safety record.
new_summary:
A 58-year-old man was arrested on Jan 19 after allegedly assaulting a 73-year-old Tower Transit service ambassador and spraying commuters with a fire extinguisher at the Yishun Integrated Transport Hub (920 Yishun Avenue 2) at around 9.30am. The victim was conscious when taken to Khoo Teck Puat Hospital with injuries sustained in the attack.

An interchange supervisor identified as Mr Faisal and bus captain Mr Zaki confronted the man and pursued him into the adjacent Northpoint City mall, where he continued spraying the fire extinguisher and threw it at a shopper. Mr Faisal rushed forward to restrain the man before police arrived and made the arrest.

The man was arrested for being a public nuisance and of unsound mind, and is under investigation for voluntarily causing hurt and mischief. Tower Transit commended both staff members for their decisive action in protecting the community, noting that Mr Faisal had previously subdued another individual using a fire extinguisher to damage buses at the same location in December 2022. Northpoint City's security officers assisted in managing the situation, and the mall confirmed it is cooperating with authorities while operations continue normally.
old_title: Bus staff assaulted and doused with fire extinguisher by man in Yishun
new_title: Man arrested after assaulting Tower Transit staff, spraying fire extinguisher in Yishun

old_summary: A Tower Transit bus ploughed into the covered taxi bay near Yishun MRT station on Yishun Avenue 2 at approximately 1pm on Saturday, 6 November, partially collapsing the walkway shelter onto pedestrians below. The bus, operating service 969, struck one of the structural beams supporting the low-rise covered linkway, bringing the roof down on bystanders in the taxi bay area. Three people — the 63-year-old male bus captain and two female pedestrians aged 60 and 64 — were taken to Khoo Teck Puat Hospital, all conscious at the time of admission. Tower Transit suspended the bus captain and issued a public apology, while LTA noted that low-rise taxi stands near bus stops are marked with yellow paint and black-striped columns specifically to prevent this type of collision. MP for Nee Soon GRC Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim visited the scene, with police and SCDF investigations ongoing.
new_summary:
A Tower Transit service 969 bus crashed into the taxi bay at Yishun MRT station on Yishun Avenue 2 at approximately 1pm on Saturday, 6 November 2021, causing the covered walkway shelter to partially collapse. Three people were hospitalised: the 63-year-old male bus driver and two female pedestrians aged 60 and 64, all conscious upon arrival at Khoo Teck Puat Hospital.

According to preliminary investigation by MP Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, the bus appeared to have struck one of the structural beams supporting the covered linkway, triggering the collapse. Eyewitness Raju Thenashkumar, who was driving past, described hearing a sound "like breaking biscuits" and observed the shelter—described as "two-storey high"—come down, with one side of the roof remaining lodged against the bus. He advised the bus driver against reversing to prevent further structural failure.

Tower Transit suspended the bus captain pending investigation. The Land Transport Authority noted that low-rise taxi stands near bus stops are painted yellow with black stripes on the first two columns to distinguish them from regular bus stops, with height-limit signage at entry points. Bus captains receive route training highlighting these structures. LTA commenced reinstatement of the damaged taxi stand.
old_title: Bus ploughs into Yishun MRT taxi stand, collapsing shelter onto pedestrians
new_title: Bus ploughs into Yishun MRT taxi stand, shelter collapses on pedestrians

old_summary: A Chinese national who murdered three women in a Yishun Avenue 11 HDB flat in 2008 has had his appeal against the death penalty dismissed by the Court of Appeal. Wang Zhijian, 48, stabbed his lover Zhang Meng 48 times and her teenage daughter Feng Jianyu 45 times while they slept, before pursuing flatmate Yang Jie — who fell six storeys to her death after Wang severed her fingers with a chopper as she clung to a kitchen window ledge. Originally convicted of culpable homicide for two of the deaths, the prosecution's cross-appeal was allowed, elevating all three convictions to murder. The Court of Appeal's November 2014 ruling confirmed Wang would hang, closing a case that had shocked Singapore with its sustained brutality and the calculated nature of the attacks across multiple rooms of the same flat.
new_summary:
Chinese national Wang Zhijian, 48, will be executed for the 2008 murder of three women in a flat at Yishun Avenue 11. The Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal against conviction on 28 November 2014, while allowing the prosecution's appeal against his acquittal in two of the three deaths, upgrading those convictions from culpable homicide to murder.

Wang met his lover Zhang Meng in China in 2005 and maintained a relationship described by the court as "passionate, tortured and at times bizarre". In 2007, Zhang and her 17-year-old daughter Feng Jianyu moved to Singapore and rented a two-bedroom flat at Yishun Avenue 11. After a quarrel in 2008, Wang stabbed the sleeping Zhang Meng 48 times in the head, neck, chest, abdomen and limbs, then attacked her daughter Feng with 45 stab wounds from the same knife.

Wang then entered another bedroom where flatmate Yang Jie, 36, and her 15-year-old daughter Li Meilin were sleeping. He slashed Li Meilin, who survived, then chased Yang Jie into the kitchen. As Yang Jie climbed out the window onto a narrow ledge, holding the laundry pole holders, Wang used a chopper to cut her fingers, causing her to lose her grip and fall six storeys to her death. Wang was convicted of Yang Jie's murder in 2012 and had appealed; the Court of Appeal's dismissal of that appeal and upgrade of the Zhang Meng and Feng Jianyu convictions to murder sealed his death sentence.
old_title: Triple murder at Yishun Ave 11: Death penalty appeal dismissed for Wang Zhijian
new_title: Wang Zhijian hangs for triple murder at Yishun Ave 11 flat

old_summary: Northpoint City in Yishun holds the distinction of being the largest shopping mall in Singapore's north, anchored beside Yishun MRT station after a sweeping 2017 expansion that transformed it into the country's first mall with an Integrated Transport Hub. Originally opened in 1992 as Northpoint Shopping Centre — the first modern suburban mall in a major Singapore housing estate — it has since grown to house over 500 shops and restaurants, a public library, a condominium, and an underground walkway to the MRT. The Yishun Public Library relocated to its upper floors, and the Nee Soon Central Community Club was folded into the development, making it a rare all-in-one civic and commercial hub. Junction Nine and Wisteria Mall round out Yishun's retail landscape, serving residents across the estate's northern and southern precincts.
new_summary:
Northpoint City, a 1.33 million square foot mixed-use development in Yishun, opened in the fourth quarter of 2017 with over 400 shopping and dining outlets across two retail wings, ahead of its original 2018 completion target. The development, which cost Frasers Centrepoint Singapore S$1.43 billion when acquired in 2013, integrates the redeveloped Northpoint Shopping Centre (opened 1992) as its North Wing with a new South Wing, and includes 920 residential units in North Park Residences, an air-conditioned bus interchange, and direct underground retail access to Yishun MRT Station.

Key tenants include FairPrice supermarket (33,000 sqf), Harvey Norman (34,000 sqf), The Rice Company performing arts organisation, and The Orange Academy childcare centre. Close to 90 per cent of retail space was pre-leased before opening. The development also houses community facilities including the Nee Soon Central Community Club (the first Community Club in a shopping mall in Singapore), Yishun Public Library, a rooftop garden, and a town plaza equivalent to 10 basketball courts.

Frasers Centrepoint's S$1.43 billion bid in 2013 was nearly 50 per cent higher than the second-highest offer, reflecting the developer's strategic commitment to maintaining market dominance in northern Singapore and the proven success of integrated developments adjacent to MRT stations. North Park Residences, 87 per cent sold, was scheduled for occupation by the fourth quarter of 2018, while the bus interchange was targeted for 2019 completion.
old_title: Northpoint City quietly became Singapore's most ambitious suburban mall in Yishun
new_title: Northpoint City opens in Yishun as northern Singapore's largest mall

old_summary: A 55-year-old Chinese national construction worker died after a steel gate frame toppled and fell on him at Block 413 Yishun Ring Road on the evening of October 21, 2024. The worker was pushing the gate when it derailed and collapsed, leaving him critically injured at the scene. He was conscious when SCDF conveyed him to Khoo Teck Puat Hospital, but later succumbed to his injuries. The Ministry of Manpower has since ordered Jin Shan Construction — the site occupier and employer — to halt all work activities pending investigation, with Nee Soon Town Council named as the project developer. The fatality marks Singapore's 25th workplace death in 2024, continuing a troubling upward trend from the same period last year.
new_summary:
A 55-year-old Chinese national died in hospital after a steel gate fell on him at Block 413 Yishun Ring Road on October 21, 2024. The worker was pushing a steel gate frame when it toppled and fell on him at the construction site operated by Jin Shan Construction. He was conscious when taken to Khoo Teck Puat Hospital by the Singapore Civil Defence Force but later succumbed to his injuries.

Police and the SCDF responded to the incident at 6.50pm. The Ministry of Manpower confirmed there was no foul play suspected and launched an investigation. A MOM spokesman noted that sliding gates must be properly designed and installed with appropriate stoppers to prevent derailment during use — a standard safety requirement that appears to have been breached. The occupier Jin Shan Construction was instructed to halt all work activities at the site pending the outcome of the probe.

This marked the sixth workplace death between July and October 2024, bringing the year's total to 25 fatalities — a significant increase from 14 deaths during the same period in 2023. Vehicular incidents, falls from height, and structural collapses remain the leading causes of workplace fatalities in Singapore.
old_title: Steel gate crushes and kills construction worker at Yishun Ring Road site
new_title: Steel gate crushes Yishun construction worker, 55, in fatal accident

old_summary: Yishun's Integrated Transport Hub officially opened on 8 September 2019, replacing the original bus interchange that had served residents since 1987. The old interchange was demolished to make way for Northpoint City, with a temporary facility near Golden Village Yishun bridging the gap during construction. The new air-conditioned hub seamlessly connects Yishun Bus Interchange, Yishun MRT station, Northpoint City, North Park Residences, and Nee Soon Central Community Club under one roof. For commuters who endured decades of open-air waiting and a years-long detour through a temporary interchange, the upgrade represents a quiet but meaningful win for the Yishun community.
new_summary:
Yishun Integrated Transport Hub opened on September 8, 2019, marking Singapore's 10th such facility and ending nearly three decades without a climate-controlled bus interchange. The hub seamlessly connects the new air-conditioned bus interchange with Yishun MRT station and Northpoint City shopping mall, creating a unified transport and retail ecosystem.

The facility prioritises accessibility with barrier-free design throughout: dedicated boarding points at each berth, graduated kerb edges for wheelchair users, priority queue zones with seating, nursing rooms and accessible toilets. It introduces Singapore's first "Heart Zones" — designated help areas for elderly and visually impaired commuters — plus a dedicated quiet space for those with special needs requiring a calming environment.

Operational features include 600 bicycle parking lots, reverse warning systems to detect bus movements and improve safety, and dedicated staff facilities including a canteen, toilets and lounge. Bus routes operating from the temporary interchange were adjusted upon opening to optimise the new hub's capacity and connectivity.
old_title: Yishun finally gets air-conditioned bus interchange after 28 years
new_title: Yishun gets air-conditioned transport hub after 28-year wait

old_summary: Police investigated a false report about a bomb at a McDon's outlet in Yishun — a hoax that, like all such false alarms, drew a real police response and potential charges for whoever made it. A small, modern entry in Yishun's catalogue of the strange.
new_summary: Police were alerted to a bomb threat at a McDonald's outlet at Block 846, Yishun Ring Road at 10.25pm on Thursday, April 20, 2023, but found no threat items after completing security checks. The outlet was evacuated and customers were restricted to takeaway only while officers conducted their investigation. A food delivery worker, Mr Zhuo, 40, noticed the heavy police presence when collecting an order and observed that staff were unusually guarded about the incident. The police are investigating the report as a case of communicating false information about something harmful. Offenders convicted of making false bomb threats face up to seven years in jail, a fine of up to $50,000, or both.
old_title: A false bomb report at a Yishun McDon's
new_title: Yishun McDonald's evacuated over false bomb threat at Block 846

old_summary: The potential redevelopment of Yishun 10, the beloved neighbourhood kopitiam and community landmark, has reignited a broader conversation about how Singapore evaluates built heritage. A commentary by SUTD's Yeo Kang Shua, published on Channel NewsAsia, argues that architectural, historical, and social value are too often collapsed into a binary conservation question — one that buildings like Yishun 10 may not survive. The piece highlights a structural gap in Singapore's heritage framework, where informal community anchors rarely meet the formal threshold for gazetted conservation, even when their cultural significance is widely felt. For Yishun residents, the discussion resonates: Yishun 10 has long served as more than a food court, functioning as a social node in a estate not always celebrated for its softer qualities.
new_summary:
Singapore's first multiplex, Yishun 10, faces demolition to make way for new residential and commercial development, reigniting a broader conversation about how the nation preserves its post-independence architectural legacy. Opened in May 1992 as a striking metallic structure designed by architect Geoff Malone to resemble "a rocket ship which had landed in Yishun from outer space", the building brought cinema into the heartland and attracted over three million visitors by the end of 1993, fundamentally democratising cinemagoing for ordinary Singaporeans. While the building sits on heritage non-profit Docomomo Singapore's list of 100 significant modernist structures, its proposed loss has exposed a critical gap in Singapore's conservation framework: the absence of a consistent pathway for buildings that hold genuine social and historical value but fall short of formal heritage protection.

Architectural historian Yeo Kang Shua argues that Singapore's heritage system, which works well for obviously monumental structures, struggles with the "missing middle" — everyday buildings through which ordinary life unfolded, such as the Buona Vista and Bedok swimming complexes, which were demolished despite their architectural merit and deep social significance. The commentary calls for a graduated approach to heritage, moving beyond rigid yes-or-no conservation decisions to allow selective retention, adaptive reuse and design-led integration, supported by tailored incentives and performance-based building code applications. The Yishun 10 case exemplifies a broader environmental and cultural imperative: in a city built on transformation, Singapore must develop mechanisms that honestly weigh trade-offs and carry forward the physical traces of its nation-building era.
old_title: Yishun 10's fate sparks rare debate on what Singapore chooses to remember
new_title: Yishun 10 redevelopment sparks rare heritage debate in Singapore

old_summary: A 35-year-old man was found lying motionless and pronounced dead at a flat in Block 803 Yishun Ring Road on the morning of July 27, 2024, after police were alerted at approximately 8.35am. A 49-year-old man, known to the victim, was arrested at the scene and is set to be charged with murder — an offence that carries the death penalty in Singapore. Blood was observed outside the unit on the 10th floor, with a crime-scene investigation team and multiple police vehicles present when CNA arrived before 11am. A resident at the opposite block reported hearing shouting between two men around 8am, while a sixth-floor neighbour said he had known the victim for over a decade, last seeing him earlier that week in the lift. Investigations by the Singapore Police Force are ongoing.
new_summary:
A 35-year-old man was found dead at a flat on the 10th floor of Block 803 Yishun Ring Road on Saturday, July 27, 2024, after police were called at approximately 8.35am. A 49-year-old neighbour was arrested at the scene and charged with murder, an offence carrying the death penalty under Singapore law.

According to preliminary investigations, both men knew each other. When CNA arrived at the scene before 11am, blood was visible outside the unit, and a crime-scene investigation team was processing the flat. The Singapore Civil Defence Force confirmed one person was pronounced dead at the scene after receiving a call for assistance at 8.40am.

Neighbours reported hearing shouting between two men at around 8am. A 12th-floor resident named Jerry said he initially thought the noise came from downstairs neighbours. A sixth-floor resident, Azamad, said he had known the victim for over 10 years, last seeing him on Monday in the lift. The suspect was scheduled to be charged in court on July 28, with investigations ongoing.
old_title: Man found dead at Block 803 Yishun Ring Road; neighbour charged with murder
new_title: Man murdered at Block 803 Yishun Ring Road; neighbour charged

old_summary: A legal dispute over a deceased mother's estate, centred on a Yishun coffee shop, has concluded with two sisters successfully winning an appeal against their brother's claim to a share of the rental income. The case involved the inheritance of a coffee shop unit in Yishun, with the brother contesting the distribution of proceeds from the property following their mother's passing. The Court of Appeal ruled in favour of the sisters, effectively cutting the brother out of the rental income stream he had sought. The outcome underscores the complexity of estate disputes in Singapore, particularly where commercial properties and family dynamics intersect, and offers a measure of closure to the sisters after what is likely a protracted legal battle.
new_summary:
A 70-year-old man's bid to claim $7 million in rent from his late mother's Yishun coffee shop has been overturned by Singapore's Appellate Division. Mr Tia Oon Lai, registered co-owner of the 30-year lease on Hiap Hoe Eating House since 1997, sued his mother's estate and two sisters in 2022 seeking 50 per cent of rent collected by Koufu from 1998 to 2018. A High Court judge awarded him 37.65 per cent in June 2025, but his sisters appealed.

In a 2-1 ruling on May 5, 2026, Justices Woo Bih Li and Debbie Ong found that his mother, Madam Su Ye Chu, was the sole beneficial owner of the rental income throughout the disputed period. The majority noted that Madam Su had consistent involvement in the coffee shop's affairs while Mr Tia's role was minimal and sporadic. Critically, when Madam Su stated in a 2015 letter that all rental income belonged to her, Mr Tia did not object despite being present at the meeting. The judges also observed that Mr Tia only filed suit after his mother's death in October 2021—placing defendants at a disadvantage—and that he took no action to claim his share after a 2018 agreement began splitting rent equally between them.

The dissenting judge, Justice Kannan Ramesh, argued the evidence suggested both parties intended equal beneficial ownership as tenants-in-common, and that limited weight should be placed on the 2015 letter. He noted that when Mr Tia's father withdrew from the business in 1997, the operation was reconstituted as a partnership between Madam Su and Mr Tia, a deliberate decision that suggested shared ownership. From July 2018 onwards, rent has been paid separately to both parties; following Madam Su's death, her share flows to her estate.
old_title: Sisters win appeal over late mum's Yishun coffee shop estate, brother loses rent share
new_title: Yishun coffee shop heir loses $7M rent claim after sisters' appeal win

old_summary: A tour bus driver was sentenced to 10 months' jail after fatally striking 18-year-old Malaysian cyclist Jeffson Tang at the junction of Yishun Avenue 2 and Yishun Ring Road on July 12, 2023. Yuan Changqing, 38, a Chinese national employed by charter firm Leisure Frontier, failed to slow down while making a discretionary left turn, colliding with Mr Tang as he crossed a pedestrian crossing with six seconds still showing on the flashing green man signal. The impact flung Mr Tang from his bicycle and under the rear of the bus; he was pronounced dead at the scene, with an autopsy confirming death from head and chest injuries. Yuan, who had prior convictions for two counts of careless driving and one count of speeding between 2019 and 2021, sobbed in court as dashcam footage of the collision was played. He was also disqualified from all driving licences for eight years.
new_summary:
A tour bus driver failed to slow down at a discretionary left turn on Yishun Ring Road on July 12, 2023, colliding with 18-year-old Malaysian cyclist Jeffson Tang, who was pronounced dead at the scene. Chinese national Yuan Changqing, 38, was employed by Leisure Frontier and driving a shuttle service linking Yishun, Canberra and Sembawang when he approached the junction of Yishun Avenue 2 and Yishun Ring Road without reducing speed, despite a flashing green man signal indicating six seconds remaining for pedestrians to cross.

Court footage showed Yuan making the left turn without slowing, striking Tang and flinging him off his bicycle into the path of the bus. Tang suffered multiple abrasions to his lower limbs and fatal head and chest injuries. Yuan stopped only after hearing a sound from the bus's rear left tyre and discovered Tang lying on the ground with blood pooling around his head. Tang's father, who was cycling with him, immediately attended to his son before paramedics arrived.

Yuan pleaded guilty to one charge of careless driving causing death and was sentenced on September 2, 2024, to 10 months' jail and disqualified from all classes of driving licences for eight years. The court heard Yuan had prior convictions for two counts of careless driving and one count of speeding between 2019 and 2021, which he attributed to insufficient rest time and packed work schedules arranged by his company. In mitigation, Yuan expressed remorse, stating: "I wish to express my apologies to the family of the deceased. It's too late to say anything else now."
old_title: Bus driver jailed after killing 18-year-old cyclist at Yishun Ring Road crossing
new_title: Bus driver jailed for killing 18-year-old cyclist at Yishun Ring Road
